news.title: Nigeria 2:1 Japan: FIFA Sends Message to Flamingos After Winning U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Nigeria's Flamingos claimed the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title on Saturday, November 7, defeating Japan 2-1 in the final held at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, Morocco, to write their names into the history books. The victory made Nigeria the first African country to lift the trophy in the history of the competition, capping off a remarkable tournament run that included a 3-1 semi-final win over Brazil. As seen on FIFA's official website, Nigeria took control of the match before half-time when Awawu Bashiru struck from distance in the 39th minute.

news.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
news.lede: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters.

news.title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: Liberia withdraw over Spanish transit visa setback as Ghana secure French clearance
news.lede: Liberia’s hopes of competing at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico have been dashed after the team failed to secure Spanish transit visas, despite obtaining visas to enter the host country. The Lone Star Amputees were preparing for their second consecutive appearance at the global tournament, having secured qualification through the 2024 African Amputee Football Cup of Nations in Egypt. However, their journey has come to an abrupt end following difficulties obtaining the necessary transit documentation to travel through Spain en route to Mexico. The setback comes despite efforts by Liberia's diplomatic missions to facilitate the process, leaving the players unable to honour their World Cup participation.

news.title: NBBF President Congratulates Flamingos On Historic World Cup Win
news.lede: The President of the Nigeria Basketball Federation (NBBF), Dr Abdullahi Mustapha, has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their 2-1 victory over Japan to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Mustapha’s congratulatory message was contained in a post on the D’Tigres X account,…... Mustapha’s congratulatory message was contained in a post on the D’Tigres X account, where he commended the players, technical crew, Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) and National Sports Commission (NSC) for their collective efforts in securing the historic triumph. He described the victory as a proud moment for Nigeria and African football, following the Flamingos’ success against Japan in the final.

news.title: Omidiran demands sustained investment in women’s football amidst Flamingos' World Cup triumph
news.lede: The Executive Chairman of the Federal Character Commission (FCC), Honorable Hulayat Motunrayo Omidiran, has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos on their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing the achievement as a proud moment for the country and a testament to the talent and determination of Nigerian girls. Omidiran, a former member of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) Board and a long-standing advocate of women’s football, praised the players, technical crew, NFF and other stakeholders for their contributions. She also commended the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her continued advocacy for women’s empowerment and the development of girls acknowledged the leadership of the National Sports Commission (NSC) in the development of Nigerian sports. “I warmly congratulate our Flamingos on this historic achievement.

news.title: Football fans President Ogunfuwa congratulates Flamingos on U17 Women’s World Cup performance
news.lede: The National President of the Football Fans Club of Nigeria (FFCN), Ambassador Oluwakemi Ogunfuwa, popularly known as Mama Nigeria, has congratulated Nigeria’s U17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, on their outstanding performance. Ogunfuwa, a Lagos-based football administrator, commended the players and technical crew for their commitment, determination and resilience, describing their performance as a source of pride and inspiration to Nigerian football. She urged the team to remain focused, continue flying the nation’s flag high and maintain their winning mentality. The FFCN President reaffirmed the unwavering support of Nigerian football fans for the Flamingos, wishing the team greater success in their future engagements.

news.title: Football coaches hail Busari, Flamingos over historic World Cup triumph
news.lede: November 8, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports 0. The Football Coaches Association of Africa, Nigeria (FCAAN), has congratulated the Flamingos and their head coach, Busari Hakeem, following Nigeria’s historic 2-1 victory over Japan in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The association described the triumph as a landmark achievement for Nigerian football and a testament to the quality of local coaches when given the opportunity, support and confidence to lead national teams, blueprint reports. In a statement signed by its Media Director, Femi Amusan, FCAAN said the young Nigerian players demonstrated courage, determination and the Nigerian spirit throughout the competition, culminating in their victory over Japan to claim the country’s first title in the tournament.
